title: Mixed-type object hashing fallback must not run bytes through numpy astype(str)
answers: hash_pandas_object raises UnicodeDecodeError on a column with mixed types and bytes
hash_array fails on object array containing non-ASCII bytes and ints
why does b'a\x00' hash the same as b'a' in a mixed column
mixed-type values hash differently from non-mixed ones
body:
Symptom: pd.util.hash_pandas_object / hash_array on an object column mixing types (e.g. ints, None and non-ASCII bytes like b"\xff1") raised UnicodeDecodeError whatever `encoding` was passed. Also, b"a\x00" hashed the same as b"a", and ASCII bytes changed hash under encodings such as cp500.
Root cause: pandas/core/util/hashing.py:_hash_ndarray. When hash_object_array raises TypeError (mixed types), the fallback ran `vals.astype(str)`. numpy can only decode bytes as ASCII there, and it drops trailing NULs.
Fix pattern: in the mixed-type fallback, build a bool mask of `isinstance(val, bytes)`, copy vals, and apply astype(str) only to the non-bytes elements. bytes elements go to hash_object_array unchanged, so they hash exactly as they do in a non-mixed array.
Constraints: this changes hash values only for bytes that astype(str) used to alter. Hashes of all other inputs that already worked must stay the same, because hashes are a stable public output. Any future change to this fallback must keep "a value hashes the same in a mixed array as in a non-mixed one". Tests: pandas/tests/util/test_hashing.py:test_hash_array_mixed_bytes compares the mixed array against a non-mixed equivalent with categorize True/False and several encodings.
